variants: A2 Ultra and A2 Lite on the product page's own parameter table and in AgiBot's store, which sells both with a stated price and an add-to-cart control. The maker's document centre and product pages also name an A2 Max, an A2 Pro, and an A2-W, the last a wheeled dual-arm robot documented on its own page, which this record does not cover.
availability_note: AgiBot's store lists the A2 Ultra and the A2 Lite with a stated price, a quantity control and an add-to-cart button, and states a shipping cost band, with customs duty left to the buyer. The product page itself closes with Contact us and a one-to-one customised-service form rather than a price.

named_models.name: ActionGPT
named_models.role_note: AgiBot's product page says ActionGPT generates human-like natural movements based on voice commands and intent, supporting light operational tasks.

named_models.name: HIMUS
named_models.role_note: AgiBot's product page expands HIMUS as its High-performance Multimodal Mapping System 3D-SLAM algorithm and says the system uses it for L4-level autonomous mobility with low latency and minimal drift in complex, dynamic environments.

named_models.name: VectorFlux
named_models.role_note: AgiBot's product page names VectorFlux as its planning and control algorithm, used with HIMUS for autonomous mobility.

named_models.name: RTMOF
named_models.role_note: AgiBot's product page expands RTMOF as its Real-Time Robust Motion Framework, says it applies non-linear model predictive control together with reinforcement learning algorithms and a dynamic planning engine, and says the result quickly generates globally optimal trajectories and improves motion strategies in uncertain environments.

hardware.sensors: An interactive screen, LiDAR, a microphone, a dexterous hand, two RGB-D cameras, a fisheye camera, a speaker, and force/torque sensors. The A2 Ultra page's parameter table lists a 3D LiDAR and an RGB-D camera under its perception system.
hardware.actuation: 40 degrees of freedom plus active DoF, on what the page calls a universal humanoid skeletal structure with a modular design and customizable exterior options. The page says the self-developed integrated joint delivers peak torque of 512 Nm. The A2 Ultra page's table gives the A2 Ultra as 40 total DoF with 2 neck, 7 per arm, 6 per leg, and a 6-DoF dexterous hand.
hardware.power: A 700 Wh battery with about 2 hours of runtime and battery-swapping support.

developer_access: AgiBot's own open-source Link-U OS documents a route for running the reader's own policy on the A2. Its Link-U OS Alpha documentation states the platform is based on the production-proven full-size Agibot Expedition A2, gives an all-in-one toolchain on MuJoCo and Isaac Gym covering training, simulation verification and real robot deployment, trains locomotion with PPO, and states that a single policy codebase runs across MuJoCo simulation and real robots. Its deployment guide targets the Agibot Expedition A2 Flagship Edition, and its rl_deploy repository publishes an aimrl_sdk Python package that streams observation frames from the arm, leg and IMU topics and publishes joint commands for Python-side policy deployment. The guide's user levels name hardware developers with A2 robots for hands-on development and verification. No X2 or A3 equivalent was found.
terms_note: AgiBot's store publishes Terms of Service last updated 2026-02-04, covering access, payment, shipping, returns and liability, alongside separate shipping, refund and privacy policies. No SDK or software licence for the A2 was found at review time; the maker's open-source Link-U OS carries its own Mulan PSL v2 licence, which the maker's product pages do not reference.
not_verified: The four named components and the Link-U OS policy route are AgiBot's own claims; the Atlas has not verified them. Every source is an AgiBot web page or a repository file AgiBot can change at any time.
